title: I used AI-assisted development to turn my Cyberpunk VR troubleshooting scripts into a full Windows companion app
author: ChimichangaSandwich
selftext:
**TL;DR:** I’m not a traditional software developer. I used AI extensively as a development partner to turn a collection of scripts I made for my Cyberpunk 2077 VR setup into a complete Windows companion application. I personally drove the requirements, testing and validation throughout the project, and I’d love feedback from people who are also building real software/gaming tools with AI.

I recently started experimenting with **iPowerTech’s Cyberpunk 2077 VR port** and kept running into things I wanted to automate — graphics profiles, configuration recovery, VR/flatscreen switching, hardware detection, troubleshooting, etc.

What started as a handful of scripts eventually became **Cyberpunk VR Companion**.

It now handles things like:  
hardware / HMD / OpenXR detection  
graphics profile generation and editing  
assisted performance tuning  
Smart Launch and launch-readiness repair  
VR ↔ flatscreen switching  
health checks and diagnostics  
community profile import/export  
native OpenXR stereo startup presentation

The interesting part for me has been the **development process**.

Rather than asking an AI to “make me an app” and uploading the result, I treated the process more like iterative engineering:  
**problem → design → implementation → test → failure → diagnose → revise → validate**

There were plenty of failures along the way — broken integrations, profile bugs, installer issues, OpenXR problems, render-target failures, onboarding edge cases, clean-install testing, uninstall testing, etc.  
I was the one actually running and validating everything on the machine/VR headset while AI helped with architecture, implementation, debugging and documentation.  
Eventually I reached a point where I trusted the build enough to package it as a public v1.1.0 release.  
I’m particularly interested in feedback from people here on a few things:

**How do you personally decide when an AI-assisted application is “validated enough” to release publicly?**  
**What would make you trust—or distrust—a compiled utility built with substantial AI assistance?**  
**For those building larger AI-assisted projects, how do you keep the AI from drifting away from the architecture as the project grows?**

I’m recording a video about the entire development process tomorrow, so any questions or concerns people here raise would actually be useful things for me to address.  
Project / screenshots / documentation are here if anyone wants context:  
[https://github.com/SaveTheLlama/CyberpunkVRCompanion](https://github.com/SaveTheLlama/CyberpunkVRCompanion)

comments.author: revel911
comments.body: Love cyberpunk and need a reason to jump back in via vr

replies.author: ChimichangaSandwich
replies.body: Cyberpunk in VR has been incredible! Definitely still needs some improvement but it’s heading in the right direction! If you happen to use the companion app alongside a vr port let me know how it goes for you!

replies.author: revel911
replies.body: Think there is a way to have the app auto change quality based on FPS?

replies.author: ChimichangaSandwich
replies.body: That’s something I can certainly look into! Today when I get some time I’ll look into it and keep you updated

replies.author: ChimichangaSandwich
replies.body: I apologize for the delayed update. Here’s the current state: I have uploaded the proper files to the GitHub as a prerelease that allow the ability to utilize auto quality. It will have to be enabled via the CET menu in game. One issue that I’ve encountered during this update process, with the Auto Quality in place, the ray tracing profile can no longer be launched via the companion app as it is causing a crash before the main menu. I have worked extensively to attempt to fix this however I currently have not had success. If Ray Tracing is desired a profile, it can still be applied via the CET menu in game as well. If the Ray Tracing profile is being used, auto quality will not switch to a lower profile as it causes the game to crash upon applying. I am still actively working on fixing these issues
